lines.text: My brother put on a beanie at seven this morning. He has not been the same since.
Morning is just night that woke up early.
See? Yesterday he cried at a cereal commercial.
Good morning. It is sixty two degrees in this house. Nobody is allowed to touch me.
Tyler. Do you want eggs?
Eggs are just chickens that never got a chance, my guy.
You ate nine eggs last night. Standing up. In your underwear.
That was a different man. He did not have the beanie.
I have seen this before. It always starts with the slow nod.
Mm.
That is it. That is the nod. He nods at everything now.
I told him the toaster was on fire. He nodded.
Fire is just the toaster expressing itself.
The toaster is fine. The toast is not.
Then he leaned on the fridge. For forty minutes.
The fridge leans back, my guy. It is a relationship.
He is leaning on it right now. The ice maker is scared.
I take my coffee black now.
Since when?
Since seven.
You put eleven sugars in it. I watched you.
Black on the outside. Sweet on the inside. Like the beanie.
The beanie is gray.
I fix bikes now too.
You do not own a bike.
That is why I am so good at it. Nothing has broken yet.
He also learned guitar this morning.
One chord. But I play it like I mean it.
He played it for three hours. The neighbors left a note.
The note said keep going.
The note said we are moving.
What is all this noise? Who keeps opening the fridge?
Ray.
Did my son just call me Ray?
Since seven, Dad.
Ray, my guy. The cold is just the house telling you a secret.
The cold is me. I set the thermostat to sixty two.
He did. He whispered to me. It was a little strange.
Can you please make him take it off? He wore it in the shower.
The beanie stays on. The beanie is not a hat. The beanie is a way of living.
Son. Where did you find that beanie?
The back of the closet. Behind the waffle maker nobody uses.
That is my beanie. From nineteen ninety four.
Your beanie? You wear a fanny pack to the grocery store.
I wore that beanie for one winter. Everybody called me Big Ray.
Big Ray. I have heard stories. None of them make sense.
I said deep things at the ice rink. Your mother fell in love with me there.
Mom said she fell on the ice and you were the only one near her.
Same thing.
Your grandpa wore it too. He talked like this for the whole winter of nineteen seventy one.
So why put it in the back of the closet?
I did not. I put it there every November. Then I make the house very, very cold.
Sixty two degrees. A trap. And I was part of it.
You froze us for a hat?
I wanted somebody to be Big Ray again. Your brother was ready.
Thanks, Ray.
Call me Dad. Big Ray only answers in winter.
Fine. I am turning the heat up. Give me the beanie, I am putting it back.
It does not go back. It chooses.
It is a hat, Tyler.
Okay. Fine. I am trying it on. Only to prove a point.
Mm.
Eggs are just chickens that never got a chance.
It chose.
Sixty two degrees. Another one lost. I am going to need a scarf.
